intro: People remove tattoos for many reasons: a name that no longer fits, a design done in a hurry, a job that requires a clear medical, or a wedding where family will see it for the first time. In Pune we regularly see candidates for the armed forces, police and airlines who need visible tattoos removed before a physical examination.

Laser tattoo removal works by delivering extremely short pulses of light that shatter ink particles into fragments small enough for the body's immune system to clear. Black ink responds best; green, blue and yellow inks are harder and may not clear fully. Professional tattoos with dense ink need more sessions than amateur ones.

On Indian skin, Fitzpatrick type IV to V, settings must be lower and sessions more frequent to protect the surrounding pigment, which means a longer course. At our Kalyani Nagar clinic, tattoo removal is performed on the Qyros Q-switched Nd:YAG, which uses 1064 nm for black, blue and dark brown ink, 532 nm for red, purple, orange and light brown, and 585 and 650 nm handpieces for sky blue and green. Dr. Daksha Patel, an MD dermatologist, assesses the tattoo, does a test patch, and gives you a realistic estimate of sessions and outcome before the first full session.
whoIsItFor: Small to medium black or dark-blue tattoos on the arms, hands, neck or back
Candidates who need a tattoo cleared or faded for an employment or armed-forces medical
Fading an old tattoo before a cover-up
Name tattoos and designs that no longer fit
Raised or itchy tattoos, which need evaluation for allergy before laser

howItWorks.title: Assessment and test patch
howItWorks.description: Ink colours, depth, age and your skin tone are assessed. A small test area is treated first to confirm how your skin and the ink respond.

howItWorks.title: The session
howItWorks.description: Numbing cream is applied, goggles are worn, and the laser is passed over the tattoo. The area turns white briefly (frosting) and the session takes 10 to 30 minutes depending on size.

howItWorks.title: Healing
howItWorks.description: Expect redness, swelling and sometimes small blisters for a week. The skin heals over 1 to 2 weeks while the body clears the shattered ink.

howItWorks.title: Repeat sessions
howItWorks.description: Sessions are spaced 6 to 8 weeks apart to allow clearance and healing. Fading becomes visible after 2 to 3 sessions.

sessionsAndDowntime.downtime: 5–10 days of redness, swelling or small blisters
sessionsAndDowntime.results: Fading visible after 2–3 sessions; a full course takes 12–18 months

aftercare: Keep the area clean and dry for 48 hours, then apply the ointment advised until healed.
Do not pick blisters or scabs; let them heal to avoid scarring and pigment change.
Keep the area covered from the sun or use sunscreen once healed, between every session.
Avoid swimming pools, gyms and tight clothing over the area for a week.

faqs.q: Will the tattoo be removed completely?
faqs.a: Most black tattoos fade substantially, often to the point where they are not noticeable. Some inks, especially green and yellow, resist treatment, and a faint shadow can remain. We give you an honest estimate after the test patch.
It feels like hot rubber-band snaps. Numbing cream makes it tolerable, and sessions are short.
Scarring is uncommon with correct settings and aftercare. On Indian skin the more likely issue is temporary lightening or darkening of the treated area, which usually settles over months.

faqs.q: How many sessions does a small black tattoo need?
faqs.a: Typically 6 to 10 sessions spaced 6 to 8 weeks apart. Amateur tattoos with less ink may clear sooner; dense professional work takes longer.

Black and dark blue respond best, and red responds well. Green and sky blue are the hardest colours; the Qyros has dedicated 650 nm and 585 nm handpieces for them, so more colours can be treated than with a standard two-wavelength laser, though some inks still only fade. This is assessed at consultation.
